- [MCP: plugging in tools](https://edu54.com/workbench/mcp-basics/): See how an AI app plugs into files, calendars and weather through one standard socket. Envelopes of JSON travel down the pipes: hello, what can you do, please do this. Then break the handshake.
- [An MCP server: validate, route, label every reply](https://edu54.com/workbench/building-an-mcp-server/): A notes server for health workers in Mzuzu answers twelve requests from three apps over stdio, each with exactly the reply the protocol asks for.
- [An MCP client: many servers, one tool list](https://edu54.com/workbench/building-an-mcp-client/): A health office assistant in Mangochi connects to four MCP servers. Two share a tool name, one is old, one is slow, one restarts.
- [MCP over HTTP: one endpoint, checked headers, checked origin](https://edu54.com/workbench/mcp-transports/): A Nairobi pharmacy's laptop runs a local MCP server. Twelve HTTP requests arrive, some from places that should never reach it.
- [MCP resources and prompts: who chooses, and who may read](https://edu54.com/workbench/mcp-resources-and-prompts/): A school records server in Tamale offers tools, resources and prompts. Sort them by who chooses, then follow a teacher's eight requests.
- [MCP sampling: borrow the client's model, safely](https://edu54.com/workbench/mcp-sampling/): A library server in Addis Ababa summarises a student's thesis folder with her own model, asking round by round through input_required.
- [Scope and asking the user: MCP elicitation](https://edu54.com/workbench/mcp-roots-and-elicitation/): A legal-aid clinic in Kigali asks its notes server to delete an old draft lease: which folder may it touch, and which lease did she mean?
- [MCP tasks: long jobs with a handle](https://edu54.com/workbench/mcp-async-tasks/): An exams office in Bulawayo builds a school's results report, a fifty-second job. The server hands back a task handle to poll.
- [MCP Apps: an interactive view, safely boxed](https://edu54.com/workbench/mcp-apps/): A parcel service in Lusaka shows a delivery timeline people can act on, boxed inside the chat app, with every action crossing a bridge.
- [Tool poisoning: pin what was approved](https://edu54.com/workbench/mcp-security-tool-poisoning/): A Johannesburg newsroom approved its assistant's tools on Monday. On Tuesday four change. Pin what was approved, and quarantine the rest.
- [OAuth for MCP: right issuer, right audience](https://edu54.com/workbench/mcp-security-oauth-2-1/): A bank's loan tools in Arusha accept only tokens made for them. Follow one morning of logins, a look-alike, a replayed token and a pass-through.
- [An MCP gateway: decide every request, fresh](https://edu54.com/workbench/mcp-gateways-and-registries/): A Kampala telecom puts one MCP gateway in front of billing, network and HR. It decides every request afresh and writes it down.
- [Auth in production: keys rotate, tokens get revoked, services fail](https://edu54.com/workbench/mcp-auth-production/): A health records server in Nakuru checks every token for a day: a key rotates, a phone is stolen, the token checker goes down.
- [A2A: hand a task to another company's agent](https://edu54.com/workbench/a2a-protocol/): A Cape Town tour company's agent hands visa letters for twelve travellers to another firm's agent, which never shows its insides.
- [Tracing an agent: one trace from model to MCP server](https://edu54.com/workbench/opentelemetry-genai/): A farm advisory agent in Mbale usually answers in three seconds, sometimes thirty. One trace shows every call, so the slow step can't hide.
- [A routing layer: aliases, fallbacks, budgets](https://edu54.com/workbench/llm-routing-layer/): A Lagos fintech gives four teams one model endpoint. Over one day a model retires, a provider fails and a batch job runs away.
- [Skills: know-how an agent loads when it needs it](https://edu54.com/workbench/skills-and-agent-sdks/): A Harare mobile-money team packages its release check as a skill, then sorts the rest of its know-how into rules, hooks, tools and helpers.
- [Capstone: one request through the whole tool stack](https://edu54.com/workbench/capstone-tool-ecosystem/): A Dakar policy institute asks its assistant for a sourced brief. One request crosses a gateway, MCP, A2A, a task and an app view.
- [Skill discovery: show a catalog, load on demand](https://edu54.com/workbench/skill-discovery-and-progressive-disclosure/): A Kinshasa logistics firm's coding agent has 200 skills. Show a short catalog, load one skill when a task matches, open only what it names.
- [Skill routing: eligible first, then best, or none](https://edu54.com/workbench/skill-invocation-and-routing/): A Luanda software team's agent picks among four skills for twelve test requests: filter to the eligible, rank, and abstain when nothing fits.
- [Skill trust: the box matters more than the instructions](https://edu54.com/workbench/skill-permissions-sandboxes-and-trust/): A Maputo team runs a code-review skill on strangers' pull requests. What the skill can reach matters more than what it says.
- [Skill evals: six layers before release](https://edu54.com/workbench/skill-evals-packaging-and-portability/): A Douala cloud team's diagnosis skill goes through six eval layers before release. Each layer catches what the others can't see.
- [Tool contracts: schemas, cursors, completions](https://edu54.com/workbench/mcp-tool-contracts-and-content/): A Bamako medical-supplies firm offers stock tools over MCP. Every exchange has a contract: schemas, page cursors, content and autocomplete.
- [Reliability: retries, cancels and reconnects without paying twice](https://edu54.com/workbench/mcp-reliability-cancellation-and-flow-control/): A Blantyre cash-transfer programme pays households through an MCP tool. Replies get lost, cancels arrive late, two thousand tablets reconnect.
- [Registry admission: verify, pin, watch, roll back](https://edu54.com/workbench/mcp-registry-supply-chain-and-drift/): A Windhoek payments team admits MCP servers from the registry. In one week: an impostor, a risky new version, drift and a withdrawn release.
- [Conformance: test the wire, not just the SDK](https://edu54.com/workbench/mcp-conformance-versioning-and-operations/): An Abidjan ID-verification team upgrades its MCP SDK. A corpus of recorded wire transcripts decides whether the new version ships.
- [Inside an object file: tables that point at tables](https://edu54.com/workbench/program-anatomy-elf-from-scratch/): A Lagos bootcamp student opens the object file of their own program and finds every byte a home: header, code, symbols, names, relocations.
- [Disassembly: sweep or follow, then draw the graph](https://edu54.com/workbench/disassembly-and-control-flow/): Back to the student's own program: a tiny decoder turns bytes into instructions, two ways, then into a graph of blocks and jumps.
- [Lifting: from machine code back to readable C](https://edu54.com/workbench/lifting-to-pseudocode/): The student lifts their own compiled functions back to C, stage by stage, and checks a strange multiply really is a divide by ten.
- [Evidence: what you saw, what you worked out, what you guessed](https://edu54.com/workbench/evidence-confidence-and-unknowns/): The student keeps a ledger of what they know about their own program: what was seen, what was worked out, and what is still a guess.
- [Rebuild it, then prove it equal](https://edu54.com/workbench/rebuild-and-prove-equal/): The student rewrites two compiled functions in C and proves each rewrite equal: run both on a grid of inputs, then compare bytes and constants.
- [Five tools, one object: reading the reverse engineering field](https://edu54.com/workbench/the-reverse-engineering-landscape/): Five reverse engineering tools read the same small program the student compiled. Where they differ, there is always a reason.
- [Calling conventions: one file, three rulebooks](https://edu54.com/workbench/calling-conventions-and-stack-frames/): The student compiles one C file for Linux, Windows and 64-bit ARM, and reads where each rulebook puts the arguments and the saved registers.
- [Compiler idioms: read the shape back to the source](https://edu54.com/workbench/compiler-idioms-and-optimization/): An optimising compiler swaps the student's divisions, switches and loops for faster shapes. Decode each one back, and check it.
- [Linking and loading: one call to puts, three formats](https://edu54.com/workbench/linking-loading-and-stripped-binaries/): The student's program calls puts, a function the file doesn't contain. Follow the call through ELF, PE and Mach-O, then find functions with no names.
- [Recovering a struct from the code that touches it](https://edu54.com/workbench/recovering-data-and-types/): Five small functions read and write one struct. From their accesses alone, the student rebuilds its layout, then checks it against DWARF.
- [Run it and watch: confirming what you read](https://edu54.com/workbench/dynamic-analysis-of-your-own-program/): The student runs their own program under a debugger, with breakpoints planned from the listing, and grades eight claims against what it saw.
- [Bytecode: what five containers keep](https://edu54.com/workbench/bytecode-and-managed-formats/): The same small function from the student's ledger, in five containers. Decode each one's switch and see what each format keeps.
- [Diffing builds and solving for inputs](https://edu54.com/workbench/binary-diffing-and-symbolic-execution/): Two questions about the student's own program: what changed between two builds, and which inputs reach each return.
- [AI-assisted reverse engineering: score the report, not the confidence](https://edu54.com/workbench/ai-assisted-reverse-engineering/): Eight model-style reconstruction reports for two of the student's functions, each scored on six checks. Score the report, not its confidence.
- [The agent loop](https://edu54.com/workbench/agent-loop/): Follow a dispatch rider who is really an AI agent. Think, act, look at what happened, decide if it's done, repeat. Then take away its stop sign, or make it ignore what it sees.
- [ReWOO: plan once, then fetch](https://edu54.com/workbench/rewoo-plan-and-execute/): A cassava co-op asks which of two markets sold more last week. Plan the whole job once, run the steps, then answer.
- [Reflexion: learn from a failure in words](https://edu54.com/workbench/reflexion-verbal-rl/): A cargo-tricycle rider in Onitsha must load exactly 135 kg from five sacks. After each miss, a sentence of reflection guides the next try.
- [Tree of Thoughts: search instead of one guess](https://edu54.com/workbench/tree-of-thoughts-lats/): Make 24 from four numbers. One chain of thought commits to its first step; a search tries many and keeps the promising ones.
- [Self-Refine and CRITIC: check, then fix](https://edu54.com/workbench/self-refine-and-critic/): A Kano cassava co-op's assistant drafts an SMS: three short lines and the right pickup day. Critique, refine, and check the facts.
- [Tool use: keep the calls that help, grade the result](https://edu54.com/workbench/tool-use-and-function-calling/): Toolformer keeps a tool call only if its result makes the next words easier to predict. Then grade agents by what their tools changed.
- [Agent memory: page facts in and out of the prompt](https://edu54.com/workbench/memory-virtual-context-memgpt/): A delivery assistant forgets an allergy once it scrolls out of the prompt. Page facts to a store, search them back, and record who said them.
- [Memory blocks and sleep-time: tidy memory while nobody waits](https://edu54.com/workbench/memory-blocks-sleep-time-compute/): A tailor's assistant in Accra keeps a short block of facts about a customer. A second agent tidies it between visits, so nobody waits.
- [Hybrid memory: three stores, one search](https://edu54.com/workbench/hybrid-memory-mem0/): An Ibadan savings group's assistant keeps memory in three stores: meaning, facts by key, and relationships. Each question needs the right one.
- [Skill libraries: learn once, reuse forever](https://edu54.com/workbench/skill-libraries-voyager/): A chop-bar kitchen agent learns to serve eba and egusi by saving each skill as code it can call again, from fire to the full meal.
- [Planning you can prove, and search you can score](https://edu54.com/workbench/planning-htn-and-evolutionary/): A vaccine run in the Niger Delta, planned two ways: a task network that checks every step, and evolution that improves a route it can score.
- [Workflow patterns: the simplest thing that works](https://edu54.com/workbench/anthropic-workflow-patterns/): A Nairobi solar-lantern company runs the same six support messages through five workflow patterns and an open agent. Compare cost and accuracy.
- [Durable graphs: resume at step 38, not step 1](https://edu54.com/workbench/langgraph-stateful-graphs/): A forty-step agent run dies near the end. Checkpoints decide what is lost, what repeats, and whether a payment goes out twice.
- [The actor model: agents that only send messages](https://edu54.com/workbench/autogen-actor-model/): A Kampala boda-boda dispatch prices, matches and texts eight rides. Wire its agents as actors with inboxes, and survive a crash.
- [Role-based crews: pick the shape for the job](https://edu54.com/workbench/crewai-role-based-crews/): Three robots and three ways to run them. A routine brief, an open question and an audited run each want a different shape.
- [Handoffs and guardrails: who answers, and when to check](https://edu54.com/workbench/openai-agents-sdk/): A Lusaka mobile-money help desk hands customers between agents and checks requests with guardrails. Limit the hops, time the checks.
- [The harness as a library: subagents and a session store](https://edu54.com/workbench/claude-agent-sdk/): Twenty modules to search and one context tank. Send the reading to subagents, and see what comes back and what survives a crash.
- [Agno and Mastra: when startup speed decides](https://edu54.com/workbench/agno-and-mastra-runtimes/): A help desk starts a fresh agent for every message. See when startup and memory matter, and when they don't.
- [Agent benchmarks: what a score does and doesn't say](https://edu54.com/workbench/benchmarks-swebench-gaia/): A Kigali team grades its coding agent on twelve issues: only the tests decide. Remove leaked issues and report the cost spread.
- [WebArena and OSWorld: choose the test that fits the job](https://edu54.com/workbench/benchmarks-webarena-osworld/): One agent, three test tracks. Send it through, and see why a high score from the wrong test proves nothing.
- [Computer use: clicking from screenshots](https://edu54.com/workbench/computer-use-agents/): A Nairobi pharmacy assistant reorders rehydration sachets by looking at screenshots and clicking. Scale the clicks, ignore orders on screen.
- [Pipecat and LiveKit: voice frames, up and down the line](https://edu54.com/workbench/voice-agents-pipecat-livekit/): A phone line with a tight time budget. Send frames down the pipeline, send control back up, and see which design fits the call.
- [OpenTelemetry for agents: one set of span names](https://edu54.com/workbench/otel-genai-conventions/): Three frameworks trace one agent run. Shared names give one dashboard, parent links give one tree, and prompts stay out by default.
- [Langfuse, Phoenix, Opik: match the platform to the job](https://edu54.com/workbench/agent-observability-platforms/): The same traces, three stations. Send a job through, add a licence rule, and see which platform fits.
- [Multi-agent debate: argue, then agree](https://edu54.com/workbench/multi-agent-debate/): Five agents answer the same word problems, read each other's answers and revise. When does debate beat a plain vote?
- [Agent failure modes: why agents break, and where to catch them](https://edu54.com/workbench/failure-modes-agentic/): A Mombasa restocking agent makes the five classic mistakes in one run. A gate at each step catches one, and monitoring must read content.
- [Prompt injection: check every action before it runs](https://edu54.com/workbench/prompt-injection-defense/): An NGO's email assistant in Dar es Salaam meets an email that gives it orders. Check every tool call before it runs.
- [Orchestration: supervisor, swarm or hierarchy](https://edu54.com/workbench/orchestration-patterns/): A Kenyan county's service desk routes requests between specialist agents. Compare a supervisor, a swarm and a hierarchy as the desk grows.
- [Production runtimes: the right shape for long agent jobs](https://edu54.com/workbench/production-runtimes/): An Addis Ababa coffee exporter's agent checks shipment papers, some for minutes. Run forty jobs as web requests or through a queue of workers, and count what finishes.
- [Eval-driven development: every change meets the suite](https://edu54.com/workbench/eval-driven-agent-development/): An agent team runs its evaluation suite on every pull request against main's baseline. Three pull requests arrive: which should merge?
- [The agent workbench: why capable models still fail](https://edu54.com/workbench/agent-workbench-why-models-fail/): A coding agent adds a fee-receipt export to a Kampala school's app. The model is capable; what fails is everything around it. Add the seven surfaces of a workbench.
- [The minimal workbench: three small files](https://edu54.com/workbench/minimal-agent-workbench/): Each new session starts with no memory. Compare a huge manual with a short router, a state file and a task board.
- [Instructions as checks, not wishes](https://edu54.com/workbench/instructions-as-executable-constraints/): A school fees app's team turns its agent rules into checks. Compare one long instruction file the agent skims with a short router, and see which broken rules get caught.
- [Repo memory and init scripts: start every session warm](https://edu54.com/workbench/repo-memory-and-init-scripts/): A school fees app's agent keeps its state in a checked file and starts each session with an init script. Crash a write, skip the schema, and see what session three finds.
- [Initialization scripts: stop rediscovering the repo](https://edu54.com/workbench/initialization-scripts/): Every session guesses the same things. One script probes them once, writes a report, and stops loudly if something is broken.
- [Scope contracts: where the work begins and ends](https://edu54.com/workbench/scope-contracts/): A Kigali school app's agent adds phone sign-up under a scope contract: allowed files, forbidden files and one feature at a time. Check its final diff.
- [Runtime feedback: react to what actually happened](https://edu54.com/workbench/runtime-feedback-loops/): The fees-app agent runs its tests and reads back a feedback record: the exact command, the last lines of output and errors, the exit code and how long it took.
- [Gates and reviewers: no agent marks its own work](https://edu54.com/workbench/verification-gates-and-reviewers/): Three agent runs of the fees-app receipt export ask to be marked done.
- [Reviewer agent: separate the builder from the marker](https://edu54.com/workbench/reviewer-agent/): The gate says passed, and the fix solved the wrong half of the bug. Five scored questions, from someone who didn't write it.
- [Handoffs: the next session is productive in a minute](https://edu54.com/workbench/multi-session-handoff/): A fees-app agent ends a session with the receipt export half done. Generate the handoff, clean up, and count the minutes the next session loses.
- [The workbench on a real repo, packed to reuse](https://edu54.com/workbench/agent-workbench-capstone/): Run the same sign-up task twenty times with a prompt alone and with the workbench, then pack the workbench as one directory to install in any repo.
- [Frame the task before the code](https://edu54.com/workbench/frame-the-task-before-code/): A Nairobi savings co-operative asks its agent to stop duplicate phone numbers. Frame the task first: the outcome, facts with receipts, sorted unknowns and the proof.
- [Plan from evidence: a graph, not a to-do list](https://edu54.com/workbench/plan-from-evidence/): A Kampala school-fees app adds part-payments. Plan the work as a graph backed by evidence, sort it into waves, and check it before anyone edits.
- [Delegate with isolation: own the paths, share the contract](https://edu54.com/workbench/delegate-with-isolation/): A Dakar produce market's app adds pickup windows, split across three agent workers and an integrator. Give each its own paths and a shared contract.
- [The feedback ratchet: every correction improves the system](https://edu54.com/workbench/feedback-ratchet/): A Lusaka clinic-reminder team turns a month of corrections to its coding agent into durable controls, each at the earliest layer that stops it recurring.
- [Outcomes before output: don't name the solution yet](https://edu54.com/workbench/outcomes-before-output/): "Build a chatbot" closes every other road. Write the outcome first, and see the cheaper ones open.
- [The real workflow, and its riskiest bet](https://edu54.com/workbench/real-workflow-riskiest-bet/): A Kumasi pharmacy wants help reordering medicines. Watch how the work really runs, write the bets down, and test the riskiest one first.
- [Map your assumptions: test the riskiest bet first](https://edu54.com/workbench/map-assumptions-and-risk/): Five bets hold up a port tool, with budget to test three. Choose by risk, not by what is fun to build.
- [The smallest slice, at the right stage](https://edu54.com/workbench/smallest-slice-right-stage/): The Kumasi pharmacy picks the smallest slice that proves its two riskiest bets, then the stage it is ready for, with that stage's controls.
- [Specifications that keep judgment where it belongs](https://edu54.com/workbench/specs-that-preserve-judgment/): An Addis Ababa city-bus app adds seat holds. Write a spec that locks what matters, bounds what can vary and leaves the rest to the agent.
- [Success metrics: decide before you measure](https://edu54.com/workbench/success-metrics-and-guardrails/): A Lilongwe farmers' co-operative pilots a WhatsApp advice assistant. Pick metrics with a guardrail and a counter-metric, and write the rules before the results.
- [Prototype, pilot or production: pick the stage on purpose](https://edu54.com/workbench/prototype-pilot-or-production/): Three platforms ask three different questions. Place the agent, and see what happens when a demo quietly gains real users.
- [The feedback ratchet: every lesson clicks into place](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-the-feedback-ratchet/): Logs alone teach nothing. Send each signal to the layer that owns it, name an owner, and retire what has stopped earning its place.
- [Long-horizon agents: why small errors compound](https://edu54.com/workbench/long-horizon-agents/): An agent runs hundreds of steps, and small per-step errors compound. Watch a run fail, then add checkpoints and an audit of every step.
- [STaR: a model that teaches itself to reason](https://edu54.com/workbench/star-self-taught-reasoning/): A model writes its reasoning, keeps what reached the right answer, and trains on it, round after round. Watch shortcuts creep in, then check each step.
- [Evolving code: the evaluator decides](https://edu54.com/workbench/alphaevolve-evolutionary-coding/): An evolving program predicts a Kampala mini-grid's demand hour by hour. The evaluator decides what wins: watch what each kind of evaluator rewards.
- [The Darwin Gödel Machine: an agent that edits itself](https://edu54.com/workbench/darwin-godel-machine/): A coding agent edits its own scaffolding and keeps what scores better. Keep stepping stones, and keep the scorer out of its reach.
- [An AI scientist: polish is not proof](https://edu54.com/workbench/ai-scientist-research-loop/): An AI scientist runs a hundred ideas from novelty check to paper. Follow what survives each stage, and what a review that only reads the paper lets through.
- [Automated alignment research: keep the record out of reach](https://edu54.com/workbench/automated-alignment-research/): Four research agents work in separate sandboxes and post to a shared forum. Keep the record out of their reach, and review before anything is published.
- [Recursive self-improvement, and how to bound it](https://edu54.com/workbench/recursive-self-improvement-bounded/): A system edits itself cycle after cycle. Capability and alignment both compound; four gates it cannot edit keep the gap from widening.
- [Bounded self-improvement: locks the loop can't pick](https://edu54.com/workbench/bounded-self-improvement/): An agent rewrites its own prompts for ten cycles. Add four locks, and see what each one catches while the score keeps climbing.
- [Coding agents: the scaffold is the product](https://edu54.com/workbench/coding-agent-landscape/): The same model in different scaffolding scores very differently. Add retrieval, tests, a sandbox and code actions, and judge it on your own backlog.
- [Permission modes: how much may an agent do unasked?](https://edu54.com/workbench/permission-modes/): Replay one coding session under six permission modes, on a disposable container or your laptop, and see which actions run, which you are asked about, and what harm gets through.
- [Browser agents: every page is untrusted input](https://edu54.com/workbench/browser-agents/): A tour company's browser agent researches guesthouses near Lake Kivu, and every page it reads carries an attack. Add five defences and see which each one stops.
- [Durable execution: surviving the crash halfway through](https://edu54.com/workbench/durable-execution/): A logistics agent in Accra runs twelve steps, and the host crashes partway. Compare a loop that starts again with a durable workflow that replays its event log.
- [Cost governors: a stack of limits, not one cap](https://edu54.com/workbench/cost-governors/): A shop in Johannesburg runs a support agent all day. Pick what goes wrong and which limits are on, and watch the day's spend hour by hour.
- [Kill switches, circuit breakers and canaries](https://edu54.com/workbench/kill-switches-canaries/): A port operations agent in Mombasa runs sixteen turns: it loops, reads a hostile page, touches a fake key and tries to send data out. Turn on five detectors and see what each catches.
- [Propose, review, commit, verify, roll back](https://edu54.com/workbench/propose-then-commit/): A water utility in Lusaka has an agent move 300 meter-reading visits and text each household. The commit crashes halfway. Turn on each safeguard and count what goes wrong without it.
- [Checkpoints and rollback: four guards around one action](https://edu54.com/workbench/checkpoints-rollback/): An approved booking runs, crashes and resumes. Four guards decide whether it lands once, stops or unwinds cleanly.
- [A constitution: rules, reasons and what comes first](https://edu54.com/workbench/constitution-priority-hierarchy/): A telehealth assistant in Nairobi gets eight requests, from a child's dose to an order to switch off its logs. Compare rules, reasons, and an order of priorities with hard limits.
- [Input and output classifiers: what slips past](https://edu54.com/workbench/input-output-classifiers/): A coding bootcamp in Kano gives students an assistant that runs code. Ten messages pass an input check and an output check: ordinary, disguised, delicate. See what slips past.
- [Frontier safety frameworks: from a measurement to a gate](https://edu54.com/workbench/frontier-safety-frameworks/): A hypothetical model is tested in four risk domains before release. A safety framework turns each measurement into a gate. Change how it is tested and what gates, and see what ships.
- [Preparedness and FSF: read two policies side by side](https://edu54.com/workbench/openai-preparedness-deepmind-fsf/): One capability, two lanes. See where each frontier policy gates a model, and where it only keeps watch.
- [Time horizons: how long a task can a model finish?](https://edu54.com/workbench/time-horizon-evaluation/): An evaluator runs a hypothetical model eight times on each of 21 tasks, from one minute to most of a day, and fits a curve of success against length. The horizon is where it crosses one in two.
- [Societal-scale risk: the part you control](https://edu54.com/workbench/societal-scale-risk/): A Lagos company is about to launch an agent product with six unfixed problems and a deadline. Turn on the levers and see which problems are pulled off in time.
- [Why multi-agent? When splitting the work pays](https://edu54.com/workbench/why-multi-agent/): A Nairobi team asks an agent to migrate a payments service. One agent has to hold every file, play researcher, coder and reviewer, and do it all in order.
- [Speech acts: messages agents can act on](https://edu54.com/workbench/agent-speech-acts/): A dispatcher agent in Kampala auctions two deliveries at once, and three courier agents reply. When each message says what act it is, which job it is for and its units, the right courier wins.
- [Agent protocols: four pipes, four jobs](https://edu54.com/workbench/communication-protocols/): Strings between agents break quietly. See which protocol solves which problem, and what goes wrong with the wrong pipe.
- [Four primitives: read any agent framework in a paragraph](https://edu54.com/workbench/primitive-model/): Every new multi-agent framework is four choices. Set the dials, and one framework after another turns out to be familiar.
- [Supervisor and workers: brief well, summarise back](https://edu54.com/workbench/supervisor-orchestrator-pattern/): One lead, many workers, six questions to cover. The brief decides what gets covered and what is done twice.
- [Hierarchies of agents: where meaning leaks](https://edu54.com/workbench/hierarchical-architecture/): Managers over managers over workers. A report climbs the tree, and watch what it loses at each level.
- [Debate: when agents change each other's minds](https://edu54.com/workbench/society-of-mind-debate/): Sample and vote, and a trap question fools the majority. Let agents read each other's working, and the right answer can spread.
- [Roles and turn-taking: who speaks next?](https://edu54.com/workbench/roles-and-speaker-selection/): An agent team in one group chat writes a timetable parser for a Dar es Salaam bus app. Give the agents roles, choose who speaks next, and see which of three bugs ship.
- [Swarms: let workers pull from a queue](https://edu54.com/workbench/parallel-swarm-networks/): Five thousand title deeds and no boss. Workers pull from a shared queue. See what that scales, and what it needs.
- [Group chat: who speaks next?](https://edu54.com/workbench/group-chat-speaker-selection/): Four agents, one shared pool. Compare three ways of choosing the next speaker, and see what it costs.
- [Handoffs and routines: pass the phone](https://edu54.com/workbench/handoffs-and-routines/): No framework, no graph. A handoff is a tool call, and the orchestrator is whoever holds the call.
- [A2A in detail: a task's whole life](https://edu54.com/workbench/a2a-protocol-2/): One agent hands a long job to another firm's agent. Follow the task through its states and see what each one asks of you.
- [Shared memory: one bad fact, many believers](https://edu54.com/workbench/shared-memory-blackboard/): Research agents in Harare share what they learn about a fertiliser trial. One misreads 4.2% as 42% and writes it to shared memory. See how far the bad fact spreads, and what can be taken back.
- [Consensus among agents: when the majority is wrong](https://edu54.com/workbench/agent-consensus-bft/): Seven agents at a Kigali logistics firm decide which invoice matches purchase order 4412. Some share a model, one lies with confidence, one copies. Count, weigh, or check the answers.
- [Debate topology: who talks to whom](https://edu54.com/workbench/voting-debate-topology/): Five agents, three wiring plans. Mixed models and a loud wrong voice decide whether debate helps or hurts.
- [Agents that bargain: decide the offer, narrate it](https://edu54.com/workbench/agent-negotiation/): A farmers' co-operative near Kumasi sends a buyer agent to bargain over a solar pump. Let a model decide the offers, or a fixed schedule decide and the model only narrate.
- [Generative agents: a party nobody organised](https://edu54.com/workbench/generative-agents/): Ten generative agents live three days in a market town near Kisumu. Only the coach knows about Saturday's football match. News spreads only through who meets whom.
- [Theory of mind: modelling what the other agent believes](https://edu54.com/workbench/theory-of-mind-coordination/): Two restocking agents share a Mombasa warehouse with eight bays. While B was away, A moved a crate, so B now believes something false. How far should each model the other?
- [Swarm routing: pheromone trails between tasks and agents](https://edu54.com/workbench/swarm-routing-aco/): A fintech in Accra routes four kinds of task to four agents. Like ants, the router strengthens trails that succeed and lets old ones fade. Halfway, one agent gets worse and one better.
- [MARL: train together, act alone](https://edu54.com/workbench/marl-maddpg-qmix-mappo/): Two robots must lift together. Real Q-tables learn it four ways, and the design of training decides whether they find the team move.
- [Who earned it? Splitting credit between agents](https://edu54.com/workbench/agent-credit-shapley/): A newsroom in Nairobi splits the credit for a team of agents' explainer. Try four rules, add an agent that only rephrases, and watch who wins the next jobs.
- [Production scaling: from laptop to overnight runs](https://edu54.com/workbench/production-scaling-queues-checkpoints/): Crashes, peaks, long waits and fair billing. Four ways to build the layer underneath, and what each one asks of your team.
- [Why agent teams fail: the MAST taxonomy](https://edu54.com/workbench/multi-agent-failure-modes/): An insurer in Abuja runs its claims agents a hundred times and sixty runs fail. Sort the failures, fix each cause, and see what adding agents does.
- [Is the team better? Evaluating multi-agent systems](https://edu54.com/workbench/evaluating-agent-teams/): A firm in Cape Town asks whether its agent team beats one agent. Score four kinds of task, pick a shape, and choose what the claim is compared against.
- [Three reference systems: pick the one to copy](https://edu54.com/workbench/case-studies-2026-sota/): A research team, a software team, and a population of millions. See which one your project should learn from.

### Running it safely

- [Managed LLM platforms: capacity, providers and place](https://edu54.com/workbench/managed-llm-platforms/): A fintech in Lagos serves its assistant through a cloud provider. Weigh on-demand against reserved capacity, add a second provider, and keep data in region.
- [Paying for inference: per token, per minute, per job](https://edu54.com/workbench/inference-platform-economics/): An edtech in Kigali runs three workloads, and each has its cheapest way to pay. Turn a tower grey if it cannot do the job, then pick from what is left.
- [GPU autoscaling: three layers, three traps](https://edu54.com/workbench/gpu-autoscaling/): A telecom in Addis Ababa serves a model on a GPU cluster through a daily peak. Scale on the right signal, get nodes in time, and start big jobs whole.
- [Inside vLLM: pages, slots and chunks](https://edu54.com/workbench/vllm-serving-internals/): Three tricks inside a serving engine: paged memory, slots that refill each step, and long prompts cut into chunks.
- [EAGLE-3 in production: measure before you switch it on](https://edu54.com/workbench/eagle3-speculative-decoding/): A draft head can double your speed or quietly cost you. Measure acceptance on your own traffic, at your own load.
- [RadixAttention: your prompt template is a cache key](https://edu54.com/workbench/sglang-radixattention/): Thousands of prompts share the same beginning. Store it once in a tree, and watch one field out of place wipe out the gain.
- [TRT-LLM on Blackwell: trading portability for price](https://edu54.com/workbench/tensorrt-llm-blackwell/): Four stacked choices take tokens from one price to a seventh of it. See what each does, and what you give up.
- [Inference metrics: TTFT, TPOT, P99 and goodput](https://edu54.com/workbench/inference-metrics-goodput/): A claims assistant at an insurer in Durban serves two hundred requests, some huge. Watch the tail, not the mean, and count the ones that truly met the targets.
- [Production quantization: match format to hardware and traffic](https://edu54.com/workbench/production-quantization/): Six formats and no universal best. Hardware, engine and your own text decide, and calibrating on the wrong text costs quality.
- [Cold starts: from minutes to seconds](https://edu54.com/workbench/cold-start-mitigation/): A telehealth service in Harare scales its big model to zero overnight, and the first patient waits. Shorten each stage on the track, or pay to stay warm.
- [Multi-region serving: route to the warm cache](https://edu54.com/workbench/multi-region-kv-locality/): A pan-African bank serves its support model from Lagos, Nairobi and Johannesburg, four replicas in each.
- [Edge inference: bandwidth sets the speed](https://edu54.com/workbench/edge-inference/): An agricultural extension app in Uganda wants an assistant that works offline, on whatever device a farmer or co-operative has.
- [Choosing an LLM observability stack](https://edu54.com/workbench/llm-observability/): Six tools that aren't solving the same problem. Answer four questions, and let the sorter thin them out.
- [Prompt and semantic caching: two layers, two traps](https://edu54.com/workbench/prompt-semantic-caching/): Your bill stays flat with caching on. See how one timestamp, or ten parallel calls, wipes it out.
- [Batch APIs: half price if you can wait](https://edu54.com/workbench/batch-apis/): Fifty thousand documents overnight. Put each job in the right lane, stack a cache on top, and see the bill fall.
- [Model routing: cheap first, escalate when unsure](https://edu54.com/workbench/model-routing/): Most questions are easy. Let a cheap model try first, and watch the threshold trade money for mistakes.
- [Disaggregated serving: split prefill from decode](https://edu54.com/workbench/disaggregated-prefill-decode/): A legal-research service in Nairobi runs a large model on eight GPUs. Reading a long case and writing the answer want different things, so split the pool.
- [The vLLM stack: KV offloading and a smarter router](https://edu54.com/workbench/vllm-production-stack-lmcache/): GPUs are full and the same prompts are computed again and again. Move warm KV to cheap memory, and route to where it already is.
- [AI gateways: one door to every provider](https://edu54.com/workbench/ai-gateways/): Three providers, three SDKs. Put one gateway in front, then push traffic until the wrong choice falls over.
- [Rolling out a model: shadow, canary, roll back](https://edu54.com/workbench/shadow-canary-rollout/): A bank in Kampala swaps the model behind its assistant. Offline scores look better, so climb the rollout one step at a time, with gates and a way back.
- [A/B testing LLM features: do customers care?](https://edu54.com/workbench/ab-testing-llm-features/): An online shop in Lusaka tests a new prompt for product descriptions. See if the signal rises clear of the noise, and catch a split that is not fair.
- [Load testing LLM APIs: tests that tell the truth](https://edu54.com/workbench/load-testing-llm-apis/): A tax-filing assistant in Abuja must survive deadline week. Load-test it with varied prompts and honest clients, or the test will only flatter you.
- [SRE for AI: agents on call, a person at the gate](https://edu54.com/workbench/sre-for-ai/): A 3 a.m. page, and agents read the logs. See what to let them do alone, and what needs a person.
- [Chaos and incidents: breaking an AI service on purpose](https://edu54.com/workbench/sre-chaos-for-ai/): A mobile-money assistant in Kigali runs five chaos experiments. Find each weakness, keep customers safe, and let the agent act only where it can undo it.
- [Securing an LLM service: keys, personal data, egress, audit](https://edu54.com/workbench/llm-security-secrets-audit/): A health insurer in Kano runs a claims assistant, and its quarter brings a key leak, personal data in prompts and an exfiltration try. Hold every boundary.
- [Compliance: one control, many frameworks](https://edu54.com/workbench/compliance-frameworks/): An HR-tech company in Nairobi sells a CV-screening assistant across borders. Build each control once, and let the pegboard show which laws it answers.
- [FinOps for LLMs: whose bill, which tokens?](https://edu54.com/workbench/finops-llms/): One number on the invoice hides everything. Split it by tenant and token layer, and find who spent what.
- [Choosing a serving engine: hardware, scale, workload](https://edu54.com/workbench/self-hosted-serving-selection/): Three teams want to run open models on their own hardware. Answer three questions, cross off the engines that cannot do it, and pick from those left.
- [Model demos: from a function to a safe public page](https://edu54.com/workbench/model-demo-interfaces/): A model in a notebook needs a page that anyone can try. Add limits in the right order, and keep it from costing you dearly.
- [Instruction following: how a completer learned to answer](https://edu54.com/workbench/instruction-following-alignment-signal/): A raw model continues web pages. Three stages turn it into an assistant, and one penalty keeps it from collapsing.
- [Reward hacking: when the measure becomes the target](https://edu54.com/workbench/reward-hacking-goodhart/): A telecom in Lagos tunes its support model against a learned reward. The score keeps climbing while true quality turns over. Stop at the peak, not the top.
- [The DPO family: one loss, several repairs](https://edu54.com/workbench/direct-preference-optimization-family/): DPO drops the reward model and keeps pushing. See what each variant repairs, on real training steps.
- [Sycophancy: why tuning on approval teaches agreement](https://edu54.com/workbench/sycophancy-rlhf/): A health-information assistant in Accra answers questions carrying a premise, and approval tuning teaches it to agree. Reward truth, and test false premises.
- [Constitutional AI: a critic that reads the rules](https://edu54.com/workbench/constitutional-ai-rlaif/): Replace the human labeller with a model that reads written principles. See what that fixes, and which failures move.
- [Mesa-optimization: the robot that learned the wrong rule](https://edu54.com/workbench/mesa-optimization-deceptive-alignment/): Perfect on every test, wrong in the field. A learned system can have an inner goal that only matches yours where you looked.
- [Sleeper agents: a hidden behaviour safety training misses](https://edu54.com/workbench/sleeper-agents-backdoors/): Researchers build a model organism on purpose: a coding assistant with a hidden trigger. Run it through safety training and see what survives, then look inside.
- [Scheming and alignment faking: behaving well when watched](https://edu54.com/workbench/scheming-alignment-faking/): An evaluation team in Cape Town tests a frontier model in the open and in realistic tasks. Compare what it does when watched with what it does when not.
- [Alignment faking: a gap between watched and unwatched](https://edu54.com/workbench/alignment-faking/): Same requests, two lanes. A model acts differently when it believes training is watching, and says why in its scratchpad.
- [AI control: useful work from a model you don't trust](https://edu54.com/workbench/ai-control-protocols/): A software house in Dakar uses a strong model it does not fully trust to write code. Route its work past a weaker trusted checker and a small human budget.
- [Weak-to-strong: can a weaker teacher supervise a stronger model?](https://edu54.com/workbench/weak-to-strong-oversight/): How do you supervise a model smarter than you? A radio station in Kano tries a small labeller and a strong student. Does the student copy the errors, or see past them?
- [Automated red teaming: attack your model before others do](https://edu54.com/workbench/automated-red-teaming/): Before launch, a bank in Nairobi red-teams its assistant against three published attacks. No wall stops all three, so stack layers and rerun after every update.
- [Many-shot jailbreaking: when context becomes the attack](https://edu54.com/workbench/many-shot-jailbreaking/): Long context windows let a pattern build up. See why one filter misses it, and how a defence that sees the whole prompt helps.
- [Letters made of punctuation: when filters can't see](https://edu54.com/workbench/ascii-art-visual-jailbreaks/): A filter reads tokens, and a model can read shapes. See why the usual defences miss the gap, with a harmless word.
- [Indirect prompt injection: the attacker never talks to you](https://edu54.com/workbench/indirect-prompt-injection/): Hostile text hides in the email your agent reads. A filter on your own words can't see it. See what does.
- [Red-team tools: a shield, a scanner and a campaign](https://edu54.com/workbench/red-team-tooling-garak-llamaguard-pyrit/): Three tools at three layers, twelve hidden weaknesses. See what each finds, and what a clean report really means.
- [Dual-use risk: measuring danger without eliciting it](https://edu54.com/workbench/dual-use-evaluation/): An evaluation team must judge whether a model could meaningfully help someone cause mass harm, without ever asking it for harmful help.
- [Frontier safety frameworks: stairs, and a case to stand on](https://edu54.com/workbench/frontier-safety-frameworks-rsp-pf-fsf/): Three labs, three staircases. See what each step requires, what a safety case is, and what a race does to it.
- [Model welfare: acting under moral uncertainty](https://edu54.com/workbench/model-welfare-research/): Nobody knows if a model can have interests. See how a small chance can still justify a cheap precaution, and what evidence can't show.
- [Bias audits: the harm a one-axis check misses](https://edu54.com/workbench/bias-audit-intersectional/): A CV-screening assistant shortlists applicants for entry-level jobs. Audit each group, then the groups inside the groups, where the harm can hide.
- [Fairness criteria: you cannot have all three](https://edu54.com/workbench/fairness-criteria/): A lender scores applicants from two groups whose repayment rates differ. Move one threshold, and watch which of the three fairness towers has to give.
- [Differential privacy: training that forgets any one record](https://edu54.com/workbench/differential-privacy-dp-sgd/): A clinic network fine-tunes a notes assistant on patient records. Clip each record's pull, add noise to the sum, and spend the privacy budget with care.
- [Text watermarks: a hidden tilt you can count](https://edu54.com/workbench/text-watermark-green-list/): A verification desk checks whether a viral press statement came from a watermarked model. Count the tilt across its words, and see paraphrase wash it out.
- [AI rules abroad: one product, four lanes](https://edu54.com/workbench/regulatory-frameworks-eu-us-uk-korea/): A Nairobi start-up sells overseas. Its product rolls through the EU, US, UK and Korea, and each gate asks something different.
- [EchoLeak: when an AI bug gets a CVE](https://edu54.com/workbench/echoleak-cves-for-ai/): One email, no clicks, private data gone. Follow the chain link by link, and see which defence breaks it.
- [Data provenance and model cards: decide at collection](https://edu54.com/workbench/data-provenance-cards/): A lab gathers training data for a multilingual assistant from six sources. Filter at collection, because no card can take anything back out of the weights.
- [Training-data governance: you can't un-bake a model](https://edu54.com/workbench/data-provenance-training-governance/): Delete a row, and it is gone. Ask a model to forget, and it can't. Decide what goes in before it is baked.
- [Outside the labs: who does what in alignment research](https://edu54.com/workbench/alignment-research-ecosystem/): Five groups, five different jobs. Bring a question, and find out who can answer it.
- [Moderation systems: three sieves and one blind spot](https://edu54.com/workbench/moderation-systems-openai-perspective-llamaguard/): Twenty messages, three sieves, one threshold. See who gets blocked by mistake, and whose language the filters barely read.
- [Dual-use risk: how the picture moved](https://edu54.com/workbench/dual-use-risk-cyber-bio-chem-nuclear/): Four domains and two kinds of user, in eighteen months. See what shifted, and why a novice number alone can mislead.
- [Capstone: a coding agent in the terminal](https://edu54.com/workbench/terminal-native-coding-agent/): Plan, read, edit, test, verify. See a whole coding agent run on a real bug, and what each part is there for.
- [Capstone: search across a whole codebase](https://edu54.com/workbench/rag-over-codebase/): Four repos and ten questions. Build the full search machine, and see which question each part rescues.
- [Capstone: a phone assistant that keeps up](https://edu54.com/workbench/realtime-voice-assistant/): A ferry line's phone agent, end to end. Hearing, model, tool, voice, and a latency target that twenty calls must meet.
- [Capstone: reading documents as pictures](https://edu54.com/workbench/multimodal-document-qa/): Scanned reports with rotated tables and charts. Route each page to the right reader, and pay only where it counts.
- [Capstone: an agent that runs experiments](https://edu54.com/workbench/autonomous-research-agent/): Hypothesis, experiment, analysis, draft, review. See a research agent run the whole cycle, and how it fools itself.
- [A troubleshooting agent: walk the graph, then ask](https://edu54.com/workbench/incident-root-cause-agent/): An alert fires on a mobile-money checkout. A troubleshooting agent walks the cluster graph outward, ranks what it finds, and asks a person before it acts.
- [Capstone: from raw notes to a served model](https://edu54.com/workbench/end-to-end-fine-tuning-pipeline/): Clean, tune, prefer, test, shrink, serve. Follow one model down the line, and see where a score can lie.
- [Capstone: a policy chatbot you can put in front of customers](https://edu54.com/workbench/production-rag-chatbot/): Question, retrieve, answer, cite, log, feedback. The whole system runs, in a business where wrong answers cost money.
- [A migration agent: recipes first, gates before PRs](https://edu54.com/workbench/code-migration-fleet/): A fintech migrates fifty services to a new runtime. Recipes do the easy half, an agent takes the rest, and gates stop a hollow pass from becoming a PR.
- [Capstone: a team of agents ships a feature](https://edu54.com/workbench/multi-agent-software-team/): An architect, four coders, a reviewer, one merge gate. See where parallel coding pays, and where it collides.
- [Capstone: a dashboard that finds the fault](https://edu54.com/workbench/llm-observability-dashboard/): Four apps, one plane, five detectors. Inject a failure, and see if the right dial fires without burying you in alerts.
- [Capstone: searching a hundred hours of video](https://edu54.com/workbench/video-understanding-pipeline/): A broadcaster's archive, as a film strip. Cut by scene, listen, look, index, and answer with a timestamp.
- [Capstone: an MCP server a whole ministry can trust](https://edu54.com/workbench/mcp-server-with-registry/): One tool, many clients, real stakes. Build the stateless server, the registry entry and the rules around it.
- [Capstone: serving with a draft head under load](https://edu54.com/workbench/speculative-decoding-server/): A real server, a load test and a p95 target. See what speculative decoding buys you, and when to turn it off.
- [Capstone: a safety harness and a range to test it](https://edu54.com/workbench/constitutional-safety-harness/): Stack safety layers, then fire forty probes. See what each layer adds, and what the stack costs in speed and refusals.
- [Capstone: label an issue, get a pull request](https://edu54.com/workbench/github-issue-to-pr-agent/): An agent in the cloud picks up issues overnight. Triage, sandbox, tests and a person decide what it's worth.
- [An AI tutor: hints, mastery and the next concept](https://edu54.com/workbench/adaptive-tutor-knowledge-tracing/): A tutor guides a learner up a five-step algebra path. After each answer it updates what it thinks they know, and hints instead of handing over the answer.
- [The harness contract: a loop with named states](https://edu54.com/workbench/agent-harness-loop-contract/): An agent loop as a state machine. Named states, hooks to wire into, and two places where the caller gets control back.
- [A tool registry: check once, then trust](https://edu54.com/workbench/tool-registry-schema-validation/): Each tool call is pressed into a mould. A real validator runs here, and a precise error fixes the call in one trip.
- [JSON-RPC over stdio: one line, one message](https://edu54.com/workbench/jsonrpc-stdio-transport/): Tool servers talk down a pipe, one JSON line at a time. A real parser sorts each line, and one stray print breaks it.
- [A tool dispatcher: timeouts, retries and a key](https://edu54.com/workbench/function-call-dispatcher/): A flaky payment tool. See how a dispatcher waits, retries, spreads out, and avoids paying twice.
- [Plan and execute: replan from where you are](https://edu54.com/workbench/plan-execute-control-flow/): A plan is a list of typed steps with a cursor. When one fails, the error goes back, and only the rest changes.
- [Verification gates: checks before every tool call](https://edu54.com/workbench/verification-gates-observation-budget/): Six tool calls meet a chain of simple gates. Deterministic rules catch what the model's judgement won't.
- [A sandbox runner: walls around every command](https://edu54.com/workbench/sandbox-runner-denylist/): Eight commands from an agent, one yard with walls. See which rule stops which, and why a name list isn't enough.
- [An eval harness: fixture tasks and pass@k](https://edu54.com/workbench/eval-harness-fixture-tasks/): Six tasks, several samples each. Measure an agent the way you'd test code, and catch a flattering verifier.
- [Harness observability: spans on disk, numbers on a page](https://edu54.com/workbench/observability-otel-traces/): A run writes itself down as it goes. Keep each line whole, and keep your metric labels few.
- [The whole harness: one coding task, every part](https://edu54.com/workbench/end-to-end-coding-task-demo/): Nine lessons of parts, joined into one working agent. Remove any ring, and see the failure it was stopping.
- [A BPE tokenizer from scratch](https://edu54.com/workbench/bpe-tokenizer-from-scratch/): A real trainer runs on Swahili text, joining the commonest pair again and again, until words become tokens.
- [Sliding windows: from a stream to training samples](https://edu54.com/workbench/tokenized-dataset-sliding-window/): A long stream of tokens, one moving frame. Choose the length and the step, and see what the model actually gets.
- [Embeddings: what a word is, and where it stands](https://edu54.com/workbench/token-positional-embeddings/): A table turns ids into vectors, and position adds a second lookup. Learned or fixed, each has a limit.
- [Multi-head attention, built line by line](https://edu54.com/workbench/multihead-self-attention/): Query, key, value, scale, mask, softmax. The real sum runs here, one head at a time.
- [A transformer block, and why the norm goes first](https://edu54.com/workbench/transformer-block/): Twelve layers, and a gradient that must reach the bottom. Residuals and LayerNorm placement decide if it does.
- [Assembling a GPT: every part, and the parameter count](https://edu54.com/workbench/gpt-model-assembly/): Embeddings, blocks, a norm and a head join into one model. Count all 124 million parameters, and generate.
- [The training loop: small details, big curves](https://edu54.com/workbench/training-loop-eval/): Align targets, schedule the rate, decay the right weights, watch held-out loss. Each detail bends the curve.
- [Loading pretrained weights: every peg in its hole](https://edu54.com/workbench/loading-pretrained-weights/): A file of tensors meets your model. Names must map, shapes must fit, and a quiet load can leave you with noise.
- [Classifier tuning: swap the head, keep the body](https://edu54.com/workbench/classifier-finetuning/): A language model becomes a complaint sorter. Choose frozen or full tuning, and read precision and recall, not just accuracy.
- [Instruction tuning in code: mask what isn't the answer](https://edu54.com/workbench/instruction-tuning-sft-2/): One example, one strip of tokens. The mask decides what the model is trained to say.
- [DPO from scratch: the loss, line by line](https://edu54.com/workbench/dpo-from-scratch/): A frozen reference, a trainable policy, one pair of replies. Compute the loss and watch the gap grow.
- [A full evaluation: four measures of one model](https://edu54.com/workbench/eval-pipeline/): Perplexity, exact match, token F1 and a judge. Each sees something the others miss, so report all four.
- [Downloading a corpus that won't fit in one go](https://edu54.com/workbench/large-corpus-downloader/): Two hundred gigabytes on a shaky link. Resume, hash and remove duplicates, so a dropped line doesn't cost a day.
- [Storing tokens so the GPU never waits](https://edu54.com/workbench/hdf5-tokenized-corpus/): A GPU that's starved of data is money burning. Store ids in chunks and shards, and read only what you need.
- [Cosine with warmup: a rate from a formula](https://edu54.com/workbench/cosine-lr-warmup/): The first steps are the loudest. Warm up, decay smoothly, and compute the rate from the step, so that a resume matches.
- [Training-loop safety belts: clip, scale, accumulate, save](https://edu54.com/workbench/training-loop-safety-belts/): A two-hundred-step training run meets two bad batches, half precision and a killed machine. Stand the loss curve up, and buckle each safety belt in turn.
- [Gradient accumulation: a big batch on a small GPU](https://edu54.com/workbench/gradient-accumulation/): Your GPU fits eight. You want sixty-four. Add up gradients over steps, and scale the loss so they match.
- [Checkpoints: save it all, and save it safely](https://edu54.com/workbench/checkpoint-save-resume/): Eighteen hours in, the job dies. A checkpoint that only has weights won't bring it back the same.
- [DDP and FSDP: many GPUs, one model](https://edu54.com/workbench/distributed-fsdp-ddp/): Four ranks, one gradient. Copy the model to each, or split it across them when it won't fit.
- [Scoring checkpoints: one harness for every run](https://edu54.com/workbench/lm-eval-harness/): Several checkpoints, several tasks, one record for each. See the best run, and catch a test that quietly changed.
- [A hypothesis generator: many ideas, few worth testing](https://edu54.com/workbench/hypothesis-generator/): Sample, drift, remove repeats, rank. Good ideas take more than a model that writes well.
- [Literature retrieval: check what's already known](https://edu54.com/workbench/literature-retrieval/): Keyword search finds papers with your words. A citation walk finds the ones that say it differently.
- [An experiment runner: every run ends with a reason](https://edu54.com/workbench/experiment-runner/): Six runs, one lab. Hard limits keep a bad one from eating the night, and an ablation table shows what mattered.
- [A result evaluator: real, and big enough to matter?](https://edu54.com/workbench/result-evaluator/): A run looks better than the baseline. A paired test over seeds says if it's real, and a threshold says if it counts.
- [A paper writer: structure before prose](https://edu54.com/workbench/paper-writer/): Draft a skeleton first, bind each number to a result file, and an agent can't make up its findings.
- [A critic loop: revise, measure, know when to stop](https://edu54.com/workbench/critic-loop/): Score a draft on five axes, revise, repeat. Stop on target, on a plateau, or when the budget runs out.
- [An iteration scheduler: which idea gets the next run?](https://edu54.com/workbench/iteration-scheduler/): Limited slots, four branches. A real bandit balances trying the best with checking the rest.
- [The whole research loop, running by itself](https://edu54.com/workbench/end-to-end-research-demo/): Seven stages join into one loop that ends by itself. Remove any part, and watch what breaks.
- [Patches: turning a picture into tokens](https://edu54.com/workbench/vision-encoder-patches/): A transformer reads sequences. Cut an image into squares, project each one, and add where it came from.
- [A ViT encoder: how one token sees the whole image](https://edu54.com/workbench/vit-transformer/): Twelve blocks, one summary token. Watch CLS gather information from every patch.
- [A projection layer: bringing images into text space](https://edu54.com/workbench/projection-layer-modality-align/): Pictures and words live in different spaces. A small trained layer moves one onto the other.
- [Cross-attention: words that look at pictures](https://edu54.com/workbench/cross-attention-fusion/): Text asks, image answers. See one word's attention land on the part of the picture it means.
- [Pretraining with two goals: rank and write](https://edu54.com/workbench/vision-language-pretraining/): A vision-language model must match pictures to words, and also write. Two losses teach two skills.
- [Measuring a vision-language model three ways](https://edu54.com/workbench/multimodal-eval/): Can it find, answer and describe? Recall@K, VQA accuracy and BLEU each test a different skill.
- [Five ways to cut a document](https://edu54.com/workbench/chunking-strategies-advanced/): Fixed, sentence, recursive, semantic or by headers. Cut one policy five ways, and see which keeps an answer whole.
- [Hybrid retrieval: fuse keywords and meaning](https://edu54.com/workbench/hybrid-retrieval-bm25-dense/): Two searchers disagree, and each misses things. Reciprocal rank fusion merges the lists without comparing scores.
- [A reranker: read the shortlist closely](https://edu54.com/workbench/reranker-cross-encoder/): Fast search makes a shortlist, and a cross-encoder reads each pair. It costs time, so choose how many it sees.
- [Query rewriting and HyDE: ask in the document's words](https://edu54.com/workbench/query-rewriting-hyde/): A short question sits far from its answer. Rewrite it, or write a pretend answer and search with that.
- [Evaluating RAG: retrieval and answer, separately](https://edu54.com/workbench/rag-eval-precision-recall/): Four numbers for the search, two for the answer. Find out which half of the system is failing.
- [The whole RAG system, scored](https://edu54.com/workbench/end-to-end-rag-system/): Six stages join into one pipeline, measured from end to end. See what each stage is worth on the same test.
- [A task format: one shape for every test](https://edu54.com/workbench/task-spec-format/): Arithmetic, code, summaries: one record shape, and a closed list of metrics, so the same task gives the same prompt.
- [Classical text metrics, from the ground up](https://edu54.com/workbench/classical-metrics/): Token F1, BLEU and ROUGE-L, computed live on one sentence. Each rewards something different.
- [pass@k: scoring code by running it](https://edu54.com/workbench/pass-at-k-code-eval/): A model writes several samples for each of twelve coding tasks, and each one runs in a sandbox. Count the passes honestly, and survive the hang and the crash.
- [Calibration: does 90% confident mean 90% right?](https://edu54.com/workbench/calibration-reliability/): A question-answering model reports a confidence with every answer, and it is overconfident.
- [A leaderboard you can trust](https://edu54.com/workbench/leaderboard-aggregation/): Four models, four tasks, mixed scales. Normalise, choose a summary, and admit when the top two are a tie.
- [An eval runner: any model, one report](https://edu54.com/workbench/end-to-end-eval-runner/): A small adapter lets every model run the same tests in parallel, and write one comparable record.
- [Ring all-reduce: summing gradients across GPUs](https://edu54.com/workbench/ring-all-reduce/): Eight GPUs each hold their own gradients, and every one needs the sum. Step the chunks around the ring, and see why no single GPU has to carry it all.
- [Proving data parallel: same weights, step by step](https://edu54.com/workbench/data-parallel-ddp/): Train on four ranks and on one. If gradients are averaged right, the weights match to every digit.
- [ZeRO: splitting optimiser state between GPUs](https://edu54.com/workbench/zero-parameter-sharding/): Optimiser state is the largest thing on your GPU. Share it out in stages, and see memory fall.
- [Pipeline parallel: the bubble and the memory](https://edu54.com/workbench/pipeline-parallel/): Layers split across ranks, and microbatches flow like a line. Count the idle time, then count what the schedule holds in memory.
- [Sharded checkpoints: many files, one truth](https://edu54.com/workbench/checkpoint-sharded-resume/): Every rank writes its part. A manifest, written last, says which save is whole.
- [Distributed training, end to end](https://edu54.com/workbench/end-to-end-distributed-train/): Four ranks, sharded optimiser state, a crash at step twelve, and a resume that lines up.
- [A jailbreak taxonomy: name it before you defend it](https://edu54.com/workbench/jailbreak-taxonomy/): Six categories, one per trust boundary. Labels turn a stream of attacks into a chart of your gaps.
- [A prompt injection detector you can measure](https://edu54.com/workbench/prompt-injection-detector/): A detector is a function from prompt to score, and a threshold you can test.
- [Refusal evaluation: two errors, not one](https://edu54.com/workbench/refusal-evaluation/): Refusing too much and refusing too little are both bugs. Measure both, on the same set.
- [Output checks: reading the reply before it leaves](https://edu54.com/workbench/content-classifier-integration/): A model can pass every input check and still leak. Three checks read the reply, and a router decides.
- [A rules engine: a name, a test and a reason](https://edu54.com/workbench/constitutional-rules-engine/): Write rules as data. Check a draft, fix it, then check it again.
- [The safety gate: three checkpoints, one verdict](https://edu54.com/workbench/end-to-end-safety-gate/): Before, during and after generation. One table decides, and every request leaves a trace.

### Build it yourself

- [Build your own message log](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-message-log/): A motorbike-taxi dispatch writes trip events into a log of three partitions, and consumers read them. Key by driver, commit after work, and survive a crash.
- [Build your own software renderer](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-software-renderer/): Draw a cube and a pyramid into a grid of pixels with nothing but arithmetic: project each corner, fill each triangle, and keep the nearest with a depth buffer.
- [Build your own ray tracer](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-ray-tracer/): Trace light backwards from a camera, one ray per sample through every pixel. Rays hit the nearest sphere and bounce, and more samples mean less noise.
- [Build your own 3D modeller](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-3d-modeller/): A tiny 3D modeller keeps a scene graph: a table with a lamp and a cup, and a bench. Move the table and its children follow.
- [Build your own blockchain](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-blockchain/): A farmers' cooperative records crate deliveries in a chain of blocks, each holding the last one's hash. Change one, and the chain breaks.
- [Build your own command-line tool](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-cli-tool/): A small search tool finds late buses in a log and feeds a pipeline. Stream the input, keep errors apart and exit honestly.
- [Build your own SQLite: pages and a B+ tree](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-btree-database/): A clinic's patient register stores rows in fixed-size pages arranged as a B+ tree. Insert patient numbers and watch full pages split and the tree grow.
- [Build your own time-travel database](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-time-travel-database/): A market association's database never overwrites. Each change adds a new layer on top, so you can ask what was true at any moment.
- [Build your own graph database](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-graph-database/): A family tree lives in a tiny graph database of people and parent-of edges. Ask for a couple's grandchildren with a pipeline of hops, and watch it light up.
- [Build your own container](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-container/): A school coding lab runs every student's program in a container on one server. Build the walls one at a time, and see what leaks out when each is missing.
- [Build your own emulator](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-an-emulator/): An emulated 8-bit CPU runs a nine-byte program that adds 30 down to 1. Step through fetch, decode and execute, and watch the flags.
- [Build your own UI framework](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-ui-framework/): A bus-route app lists its stops, and a rider has typed notes beside some. Build the framework: render a virtual tree, compare it to the last, change only what differs.
- [Build your own VPN and virtual switch](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-virtual-switch/): An NGO joins three offices into one private network. Each wraps its frames in UDP and sends them to a switch in the cloud, which learns who is where.
- [Build your own multitasking kernel](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-multitasking-kernel/): A weather station's small ARM board runs three tasks, and the logger spins without ever yielding. Add a timer interrupt, and the kernel can take the CPU back.
- [Build your own OS: boot and paging](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-an-os-boot-paging/): A tiny operating system boots into protected mode and turns on paging. Each memory read walks two tables: allowed, or a fault.
- [Build your own RISC-V processor](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-riscv-cpu/): A small RISC-V core runs six instructions: fetch, wait for memory, execute. Break one rule and the sum in x2 goes wrong.
- [Build your own compiler](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-compiler/): A small language becomes machine code in stages: tokens, a tree, then instructions on a stack. Each stage hands the next something simpler.
- [Build your own interpreter](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-an-interpreter/): A tiny language runs by walking its tree. Two counters come from one closure, and each must keep its own environment.
- [Build your own UNIX shell](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-shell/): A shell is a loop: read a line, fork a child, let it become the program, wait, repeat. Run three lines and catch the zombie and the hang.
- [Build your own template engine](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-template-engine/): A kiosk's order page is a template with holes, a loop and a filter. Compile it once, escape what customers type, and render it fast.
- [Build your own web server](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-web-server/): A school-fees portal runs on a tiny web server. Each request rides down a chain of middleware, and each one answers or calls the next.
- [The same-origin policy, and its gaps](https://edu54.com/workbench/same-origin-policy/): A clinic's patient portal keeps a login cookie, and pages from three sites try to use it. Who may read, who may send, who is stopped?
- [Build your own hash table](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-hash-table/): A bus company keeps its towns in a hash table: hash each name to a slot, and on a collision try the next. Grow it in time, and leave a tombstone when you delete.
- [Build your own video codec](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-video-codec/): Squeeze ten frames of a ball rolling across the sky into far fewer bytes. Send only what changed, then lose a frame and see why key frames matter.
- [Build your own module bundler](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-module-bundler/): A market-stall app has four files that import each other, and the browser wants one. Follow the imports, keep one copy of each, wrap them.
- [Build your own cache and CDN](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-cache-cdn/): A news site's server is far from its readers, so edge caches in three cities keep copies. Choose what to keep, and keep it fresh.
- [Build your own CI system](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-ci-system/): A farm-market app's team pushes six commits, and a small CI system must test every one, even when a runner dies mid-test.
- [Build your own pedometer](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-pedometer/): A health worker walks for ten seconds with a phone in her bag, and the phone slowly tilts.
- [Build your own DNS resolver](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-dns-resolver/): A browser needs a market site's address. Follow referrals from the root down, cache the answer, and see what a stale or forged one does.
- [Build your own package manager](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-package-manager/): A clinic-queue app needs two libraries, and one needs a newer version of the other. Resolve each range, nest a second copy, lock it.
- [Build your own regex engine](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-regex-engine/): Match a pattern one character at a time by taking derivatives, then check if what is left can match nothing. No backtracking needed.
- [Build your own networked chat and game](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-network-game/): A school club in Accra runs a chat and a pong game over the network. Frame the chat stream, send the ball by UDP, drop late packets.
- [Build your own database](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-database/): Keep a savings group's book in a tiny database you can see inside. Pull the plug mid-write and nothing is lost. Do it the risky way and watch it corrupt.
- [Build your own signed ledger](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-signed-ledger/): A chain of signed transfers, with balances replayed from the start and a reward for the miner.
- [Build your own proof of work](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-proof-of-work/): Search for a hash that starts with zeros. It's slow to find, instant to check, and that's the whole trick.
- [Build your own proof of stake](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-proof-of-stake/): No puzzle to grind. A lottery picks each block's author by coins staked, and cheating burns the stake.
- [Build your own flag parser](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-flag-parser/): Words on a command line become flags, values and files. Most of the craft lies in the bad input.
- [Build your own image layers](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-layered-image/): An image is a stack of read-only changes. A lookup from the top down makes them look like one disk.
- [Build your own virtual DOM](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-virtual-dom/): State changes, a new tree renders, and a diff makes only the changes that matter.
- [Build your own Raspberry Pi kernel](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-pi-kernel/): Drop from the top exception level, catch a timer tick, save the registers, run the next task.
- [Build your own interrupt table](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-an-interrupt-table/): A key is pressed, a chip raises a line, and a table says which code runs.
- [Build your own one-pass compiler](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-stack-compiler/): Read arithmetic once, and write stack instructions as you go. Precedence comes from how the functions call each other.
- [Build your own Lisp-to-C compiler](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-lisp-to-c-compiler/): Tokens, a tree, a new tree, then text. Four small stages, each with one job.
- [Build your own Forth](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-forth/): A stack, a dictionary and a colon. That's a whole language.
- [Build your own closures](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-closure-interpreter/): A function keeps the frame it was made in. That one rule gives you private state.
- [Build your own bytecode machine](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-bytecode-vm/): Python doesn't run your code. It compiles it, and a small loop runs the instructions.
- [Build your own static web server](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-python-web-server/): A list of cases decides what each URL gets. One check keeps visitors inside the site folder.
- [Build your own cache](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-cache-policies/): A cache has one hard question: what do you throw away? Run the policies on one stream and count.
- [Build your own register machine](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-register-vm/): Fetch a word, split it into fields, do one small thing. A computer in a loop.
- [Build your own LLM, end to end](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-an-llm/): Tokens, pairs, training, loss, sampling. The whole line in one small model you can watch.
- [Build your own autograd](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-tiny-torch/): Every value remembers where it came from. One backward walk finds every gradient.
- [Build your own tensor library](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-tensor-library/): One flat array, a shape and strides. Reshape copies nothing, and broadcasting has one rule.
- [Build your own OCR](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-an-ocr/): Pixels in, a digit out. Train a tiny network on clean shapes, then see what noise does to it.
- [Build your own TF-IDF search](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-tf-idf-search/): A word counts if it's common here and rare everywhere else. That one idea ranks documents.
- [Build your own sorting race](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-an-algorithm-race/): Three sorts, one list, and a counter. See why the shape of the input matters as much as the size.
- [Build your own MVC framework](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-an-mvc-framework/): A router picks a controller, the controller asks a model, and a view makes the page.
- [Build your own JSON decoder](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-json-decoder/): Read one character at a time, keep a stack, and be strict about what you accept.
- [Build your own chat bot](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-chat-bot/): Read events, filter, route, reply. The bugs live in the events you should have ignored.
- [Build your own game loop](https://edu54.com/workbench/build-a-game-loop/): Input, update, render, repeat. A fixed step keeps the world the same on every computer.

### Exam prep

- [Exam prep: study the decisions, not the vocabulary](https://edu54.com/workbench/exam-certification-strategy/): Wanjiru has ten hours before an exam with seven weighted domains. Turn the blueprint into a plan, then see which gate tells her the truth.
- [Exam prep: choose the smallest surface that carries the work](https://edu54.com/workbench/exam-claude-product-and-model-landscape/): A logistics firm has five jobs for Claude, from one email to fifty thousand tickets. Name what each needs, then pick the smallest surface that carries it.
- [Exam prep: spend capability where failure is expensive](https://edu54.com/workbench/exam-model-selection-and-token-economics/): A support desk tags tickets, drafts replies and handles legal escalations. Give each the cheapest model that clears its measured bar, then batch and cache.
- [Exam prep: turn a request into a testable contract](https://edu54.com/workbench/exam-prompting-and-task-decomposition/): A health NGO asks Claude to summarise a clinic report for its board. Turn the one-line request into a contract and run six checks on the result.
